body:
jason_support: Customer on Dedicated (us-west-2) reporting structured output validation failures after a tool call + surprising billing spike. Two request_ids they sent: req_9f7a2b (validation error) and req_9f7a2c (billing/duplicate). Model: redwood-v1-toolcall-quantized. Customer tenant: tenant-acme.

emily_eng: Can you paste the exact error payload and a minimal curl repro? Also need debug bundle & host logs.

jason_support: Error snippet from the customer (redacted keys):
```json
{"request_id":"req_9f7a2b","error":{"type":"validation_error","message":"function lookup_price returned string but schema expects object with keys ['price','currency']","schema_path":"/functions/0/returns"}}
```
Curl they used (redacted token):
```bash
curl -sS -X POST "https://dedicated.us-west-2.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v1-toolcall-quantized","input":"Get price for sku:1234","functions":[{"name":"lookup_price","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"sku":{"type":"string"}},"returns":{"type":"object","properties":{"price":{"type":"number"},"currency":{"type":"string"}}}}]}'
```

miguel_sre: Two things to check: 1) host-level logs for req_9f7a2b on gpu-host-12 and gpu-host-13 (possible kernel mismatch during quantized exec). 2) routing / retries — the billing spike suggests a retry loop. Run:
```bash
ssh ops@gpu-host-12 'sudo journalctl -u redwood-runtime | grep req_9f7a2b -A50'
rbcli trace --request req_9f7a2c --full
```

emily_eng: Also ask the customer if they used the function name exactly "lookup_price" or a synonym — we saw earlier cases where toolcall routing returned a legacy tool that emits a raw string. If their tool returns a string, schema validation will fail. Can support attach the customer's tool manifest?

jason_support: Customer confirms tool name is correct. They attached a snippet of their function implementation that serializes output as `"$price USD"` (string). So the runtime is handing back a string. Customer expects JSON object. They said intermittent 401s too when using OIDC token — might be unrelated but flagged.

sara_prod: Rolling canary in case it's a runtime regression: pinned redwood-v1-toolcall-quantized@2026-03-15T05:00Z for traffic from tenant-acme; if error rate > 0.5% for 5m we'll roll fully back. Also opening a billing review ticket. :warning:

miguel_sre: I'm generating a debug bundle now for req_9f7a2b with logs, kvcache, and routing traces. Command: `/debug-bundle create --req req_9f7a2b --hosts gpu-host-12,gpu-host-13 --include-logs --include-kvcache --out dbg_20260315_457`

jason_support: Customer asked for a minimal repro curl — I gave them the one above and they repro'd the validation error locally. They're okay to share the debug bundle. I ran the billing trace for org_84 as requested: `rbcli usage --org org_84 --since 24h` shows a burst of small requests ~2000 in a 3m window all with 200 responses but repeated request_ids pattern. Suspect client retry loop with no idempotency.

emily_eng: Good. Two parallel tracks: (A) get debug bundle + host logs to verify runtime is returning a string for that function call (miguel). (B) engagement with customer about function implementation / idempotency + billing remediation (jason + finance). If the runtime is at fault because of quantized kernel path returning wrong serialized type, we'll escalate P1.

miguel_sre: Debug bundle ready: https://internal/debug/dbg_20260315_457 (attached). I also pulled `redwood-runtime` stderr around req_9f7a2b: `TypeError: Expected dict, got str at runtime/tool_wrapper.py:248` — looks like the tool subprocess emitted a plain string and the wrapper didn't coerce. sending logs.

ops-bot: debug-bundle uploaded: https://internal/debug/dbg_20260315_457 :package: 

jason_support: Marking case P2 for now, pending confirmation of runtime bug. If miguel confirms wrapper bug, move to P0 and notify infra + oncall. Thanks all — I'll coordinate customer comms and a temporary partial refund for the billing spike until we confirm root cause. :thumbsup:
